issues.description: The template's Bitmap24.hpp declares the member 'data' as type 'int *data;', but the implementation in Bitmap24.cpp uses it as a byte buffer (new char[...] and fwrite expecting char*). The solution repository's Bitmap24.hpp correctly declares 'char *data;'. This type mismatch in the template will cause compilation errors and confusion for students (header and implementation disagree on the data pointer type).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's Bitmap24.hpp consistent with the implementation: change the member declaration from 'int *data;' to 'char *data;'. This matches Bitmap24.cpp usage (new char[...] and fwrite) and the solution reference. Ensure header and implementation use the same pointer type so the project compiles as required.

issues.description: The Bitmap24 member that stores the pixel buffer is declared with a different type/name usage across artifacts: in the template repository header the member is declared as 'int *data' while the template implementation uses 'new char[...]' (treating it as a char*). The solution repository declares the member as 'char *data'. This mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the image data buffer named 'data') creates confusion and can produce compilation/type errors or extra cognitive load for students mapping the class API to its implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the member type consistent across header and implementation in the template. Change the declaration in example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp from 'int *data;' to 'char *data;' (matching the implementation and the solution) so the class API matches its usage and the reference solution.
